issues.legal_issue: Compensation redetermined for landowners who did not seek a reference must track the compensation finally payable to landowners who did seek a reference.
material_facts: Some landowners did not seek a reference under Section 18 but applied for redetermination under Section 28A within the prescribed period.
The Collector redetermined their compensation by reference to the Reference Court’s award.
On appeal, the compensation awarded to the reference claimants was reduced by the Supreme Court, which also revised the categorisation of some lands.
The Union challenged the redetermination orders, and the Supreme Court directed the Collector to redetermine compensation by reference to the final appellate decree.
issues.conclusion: Applicants for redetermination under Section 28A are entitled to the same compensation finally payable to claimants who sought a reference under Section 18. If compensation is reduced by a superior court, excess compensation already received by Section 28A applicants may be required to be refunded.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 28A and 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the benefit given to a non-reference claimant is tied to the compensation finally payable to reference claimants, not merely to the Reference Court’s original award. The appellate decree is read as modifying the earlier decree, and the principle of restitution supports applying the same reduction to both groups to avoid an inequitable result. Union of India v. Mangatu Ram is referred to as the appellate judgment that reduced compensation in this acquisition; no earlier case is cited as a separate doctrinal authority.

predicates.redetermination_claim_by_nonreference_ow: A landowner who did not seek a reference applies to have compensation redetermined on the basis of compensation awarded to a reference claimant.
predicates.reference_award_later_reduced_on_appeal: A superior court later reduces the compensation awarded to a claimant who sought a reference.

issues.definition: When a non-reference landowner seeks redetermination and the reference award is later reduced on appeal, the redetermined compensation follows the final reference award.

issues.legal_issue: A delay-based dismissal does not prevent a later appellate reduction from being applied where the redetermination order reflected the award in force when it was made and the challenge preceded that reduction.
material_facts: The Collector made the redetermination orders in 1990 on the basis of the Reference Court’s award.
The Union filed writ petitions challenging those orders in 1995, before the Supreme Court reduced the compensation in 1997.
The High Court dismissed the writ petitions for delay.

The Supreme Court held that a further redetermination could be sought when the compensation was later reduced, and that challenging the original orders before that reduction would have been premature.
issues.conclusion: The earlier delay did not bar applying the later appellate reduction to the compensation payable under the redetermination orders.
issues.legal_principle: The redetermination orders were justified on the basis of the award then in force; a subsequent reduction by a superior court created the basis for further redetermination. Because the challenge was brought before that reduction occurred, the failure to obtain an earlier change to the orders did not prevent applying the later final decree.

predicates.appeal_from_delay_dismissal: A party appeals after a court dismisses its challenge to a compensation redetermination order for delay.
predicates.redetermination_reflected_award_then_in_: The redetermination order followed the compensation award in force when the order was made.
predicates.challenge_preceded_appellate_reduction: The challenge to the redetermination order was brought before a superior court later reduced the underlying compensation award.

issues.definition: Where an appeal follows a delay-based dismissal, the redetermination reflected the award then in force, and the challenge preceded a later appellate reduction, that reduction is not barred by the earlier delay.
